question: Under Alabama Real Estate Commission Rule 790-X-3-.03, when a licensee receives U.S. currency (cash) as trust money in a transaction, when must the qualifying broker deposit it?
choice_d: By the end of the following month
explanation: Rule 790-X-3-.03(3) states that in cases where funds received are U.S. currency (cash), as opposed to a check or note, those funds shall be deposited immediately.
source_note: Alabama Admin. Code r. 790-X-3-.03(3), live-verified via ARC's official AREC LawList/ViewLaw database (arec.alabama.gov).

question: Under Rule 790-X-3-.03, if an earnest money check is received and the contract does not state a specific time or event for depositing it, when must the qualifying broker deposit the check?
choice_c: When the offer becomes a contract
choice_d: Within 24 hours of receipt regardless of contract terms
explanation: Rule 790-X-3-.03(3) provides that if a check is received as earnest money and the contract form states a specific time or event for holding it, the check is deposited as the contract specifies; if no time is specified, the check must be deposited when the offer becomes a contract.
source_note: Alabama Admin. Code r. 790-X-3-.03(3), live-verified via arec.alabama.gov LawList/ViewLaw database.

question: Where must a qualifying broker deposit and hold trust funds belonging to others under Alabama Real Estate Commission rules?
choice_a: The broker's general operating account, clearly labeled by transaction
choice_b: Any FDIC-insured account anywhere in the United States chosen by the salesperson
choice_c: A bonded third-party title company account only
choice_d: A separate federally insured account at a financial institution located in Alabama, of which the qualifying broker is a customer with authority to deposit and withdraw
explanation: Rule 790-X-3-.03(1) requires deposit and accounting of all trust funds in a separate, federally insured account (or accounts) at a financial institution located in Alabama, with the qualifying broker as a customer authorized to deposit, withdraw, and write checks on the account.
source_note: Alabama Admin. Code r. 790-X-3-.03(1), live-verified via arec.alabama.gov.

question: Under Alabama Code Section 34-27-36(b)(8), which of the following is expressly listed as prohibited conduct for a real estate licensee regarding money belonging to others?
choice_a: Commingling money belonging to others with the licensee's own funds
choice_b: Depositing trust funds into an interest-bearing account
choice_c: Holding earnest money for more than one buyer at the same time
choice_d: Using a single trust account for multiple qualifying brokers within the same firm
explanation: Ala. Code Section 34-27-36(b)(8)a prohibits a licensee from failing, within a reasonable time, to properly account for or remit money coming into his or her possession that belongs to others, or from commingling money belonging to others with his or her own funds.
source_note: Ala. Code Section 34-27-36(b)(8)a, live-verified via arec.alabama.gov LawList/ViewLaw database (full statute text).

question: Under Alabama Code Section 34-27-36(b)(8)c, for how long must a licensee keep a complete record of funds belonging to others, showing to whom the money belongs, date deposited, date of withdrawal, and other pertinent information?
choice_d: For the life of the license
explanation: Ala. Code Section 34-27-36(b)(8)c makes it grounds for discipline to fail to keep, for at least three years, a complete record of funds belonging to others showing to whom the money belongs, the date deposited, the date of withdrawal, and other pertinent information.
source_note: Ala. Code Section 34-27-36(b)(8)c, live-verified via arec.alabama.gov LawList/ViewLaw database.

question: Separately from trust-fund records, how long must a qualifying broker or company retain copies of contracts, leases, listings, and other records pertinent to real estate transactions under Alabama Code Section 34-27-36(b)(30)?
explanation: Ala. Code Section 34-27-36(b)(30) makes it grounds for discipline if a qualifying broker or company fails to keep copies of all contracts, leases, listings, and other records pertinent to real estate transactions for a period of three years.
source_note: Ala. Code Section 34-27-36(b)(30), live-verified via arec.alabama.gov LawList/ViewLaw database.

question: Under Rule 790-X-3-.03(5), absent a dispute or termination without consummation, within how many business days of consummation of a transaction must a qualifying broker disburse trust funds to the appropriate party?
explanation: Rule 790-X-3-.03(5) requires each qualifying broker to promptly disburse trust funds to the appropriate party within 7 business days of the consummation of the transaction for which the funds were deposited.
source_note: Alabama Admin. Code r. 790-X-3-.03(5), live-verified via arec.alabama.gov LawList/ViewLaw database.

question: If a real estate transaction terminates without consummation and the parties disagree about who is entitled to the earnest money, what must a qualifying broker do under Rule 790-X-3-.03?
choice_a: Withhold disbursement unless there is a written agreement signed by all parties or a court order, or deposit the disputed funds with the court under interpleader
choice_b: Return the funds to whichever party deposited them within 24 hours
choice_c: Split the disputed funds evenly between buyer and seller
choice_d: Disburse the funds to the party the broker believes is more likely correct, then notify the commission
explanation: Rule 790-X-3-.03(5) and (7) provide that if a transaction terminates without consummation or the parties disagree about disbursement, the broker may not disburse trust funds except under a written agreement signed by all parties or a court order, and may deposit the disputed funds with the appropriate court under interpleader or other lawful procedure.
source_note: Alabama Admin. Code r. 790-X-3-.03(5) and (7), live-verified via arec.alabama.gov LawList/ViewLaw database.

question: Under Rule 790-X-3-.03(2), when must a real estate salesperson or associate broker pay over to their qualifying broker any funds received in trust for other parties?
choice_c: Within 24 hours, unless the client agrees otherwise
choice_d: By the next scheduled office audit
explanation: Rule 790-X-3-.03(2) requires each real estate salesperson or associate broker to pay over to his or her qualifying broker all funds coming into his or her possession in trust for other parties immediately upon receipt.
source_note: Alabama Admin. Code r. 790-X-3-.03(2), live-verified via arec.alabama.gov LawList/ViewLaw database.

question: When a sale involves more than one qualifying broker and a successor qualifying broker takes over managing the trust funds, what must the first (outgoing) broker do under Rule 790-X-3-.03(4)?
choice_a: Retain the funds in the original account until closing regardless of who is servicing the file
choice_b: Split the trust funds proportionally between both brokers' accounts
choice_c: Provide a complete accounting of the funds and transfer the funds to the successor broker
choice_d: Report the transfer directly to the buyer's lender before releasing any funds
explanation: Rule 790-X-3-.03(4) states that where a successor qualifying broker is to provide services on a transaction, the first broker must provide a complete accounting of the trust funds and transfer them to the successor broker, who then becomes responsible to the public and the commission.
source_note: Alabama Admin. Code r. 790-X-3-.03(4), live-verified via arec.alabama.gov LawList/ViewLaw database.

question: Under Rule 790-X-3-.03(6)(b), for a commercial lease security deposit, within how many calendar days after termination of tenancy and delivery of possession must the qualifying broker deliver an itemized notice of amounts withheld to the tenant?
explanation: Rule 790-X-3-.03(6)(b)1 requires that, upon termination of a commercial tenancy, the qualifying broker apply the security deposit and deliver a written itemized notice of any damages and amounts due to the tenant within 60 calendar days after termination of the tenancy and delivery of possession.
source_note: Alabama Admin. Code r. 790-X-3-.03(6)(b)1, live-verified via arec.alabama.gov LawList/ViewLaw database.

question: Under Rule 790-X-3-.03(6)(b)3, if a commercial tenant fails to provide a valid forwarding address and does not claim a security deposit refund or an outstanding check, after how many calendar days is the deposit or check forfeited by the tenant?
explanation: Rule 790-X-3-.03(6)(b)3 provides that any commercial lease security deposit unclaimed by the tenant, as well as any outstanding check, is forfeited by the tenant after a period of 90 calendar days.
source_note: Alabama Admin. Code r. 790-X-3-.03(6)(b)3, live-verified via arec.alabama.gov LawList/ViewLaw database.

question: If a landlord or qualifying broker terminates a property management agreement, within how many business days of the termination's effective date must the qualifying broker provide an accounting of security deposits, prepaid rents, and related escrows (with payment of funds) under Rule 790-X-3-.03(6)(c)?
explanation: Rule 790-X-3-.03(6)(c) requires that upon a management termination, the qualifying broker provide the landlord or new manager an accounting of all security deposits, prepaid rents, and other related escrows, along with payment of the funds, within seven (7) business days of the management termination's effective date.
source_note: Alabama Admin. Code r. 790-X-3-.03(6)(c), live-verified via arec.alabama.gov LawList/ViewLaw database.

question: Under Rule 790-X-3-.03(6)(a), which body of law takes priority over the Commission's trust-fund rule for security deposits on residential leases?
choice_a: The federal Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (RESPA)
choice_c: Alabama Code Sections 35-9A-201 and 35-9A-205 (the Alabama Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
explanation: Rule 790-X-3-.03(6)(a) states that for residential lease security deposits, Alabama Code Sections 35-9A-201 (Security Deposits; Prepaid Rent) and 35-9A-205 (Limitation of Liability) have priority, and qualifying brokers must comply with those statutory instructions instead.
source_note: Alabama Admin. Code r. 790-X-3-.03(6)(a), live-verified via arec.alabama.gov LawList/ViewLaw database.

question: Under Alabama Code Section 34-27-36(a)(2), when a licensee is found to have violated trust-fund handling requirements, what may the commission require in addition to, or as a condition of, suspension?
choice_a: Immediate permanent revocation with no right to reapply
choice_b: Criminal prosecution referral only, with no administrative penalty available
choice_c: A mandatory public apology published in a local newspaper
choice_d: Restitution to accounts containing funds held for other parties
explanation: Ala. Code Section 34-27-36(a)(2)d provides that the commission may suspend a license, and the suspension may continue until the licensee has made restitution to accounts containing funds held for other parties, completed required education, or both; the commission may also stay a revocation or suspension on the condition of such restitution.
source_note: Ala. Code Section 34-27-36(a)(2)d, live-verified via arec.alabama.gov LawList/ViewLaw database.

question: During an AREC office inspection under Rule 790-X-3-.09, which trust-account records may Commission staff require the qualifying broker to make available?
choice_a: The past six months of bank statements with canceled checks, recent bank reconciliations, check registers, and duplicate deposit tickets with validated bank receipts for all escrow or trust accounts
choice_b: Only the current month's bank statement for the trust account
choice_c: Personal tax returns of the qualifying broker
choice_d: Only records related to transactions that closed within the last 30 days
explanation: Rule 790-X-3-.09(2) authorizes Commission representatives, during an office inspection, to require records including copies of the past six months' bank statements with canceled checks, recent bank reconciliations, checkbook or electronic check registers, and duplicate deposit tickets with validated bank receipts for all escrow or trust accounts.
source_note: Alabama Admin. Code r. 790-X-3-.09(2), live-verified via arec.alabama.gov LawList/ViewLaw database.
